title: Sheafification preserves flatness of module presheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, let $\mathcal O$ be a presheaf of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules. Assume that tensoring with $\mathcal F$ over $\mathcal O$ preserves finite limits in the category of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. Let $\mathcal O^\#$ and $\mathcal F^\#$ be the associated sheaves, with the induced $\mathcal O^\#$-module structure. Then tensoring with $\mathcal F^\#$ over $\mathcal O^\#$ preserves finite limits in the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O^\#$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]; equivalently, $\mathcal F^\#$ is flat.

proof.text: The module sheafification adjunction [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] makes restriction a right adjoint, hence it preserves finite limits. Import Mathlib concrete abelian-group filtered colimits; together with the transitively available left-exact sheafification construction this yields HasSheafify for this small site; Mathlib then gives finite-limit preservation of module sheafification via underlying abelian sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. Together with the hypothesis on tensorRight F, composition preserves finite limits.

Specialize the natural bifunctor comparison [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] at the presheaf F. Its components are e.app (G,F); naturality is the comparison naturality at (f,id F), simplified using tensorHom_def. This gives tensorRight (a F) isomorphic to restriction followed by tensorRight F followed by a. Transfer finite-limit preservation across its inverse.

Choose the monoidal closed structure supplied by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. TensorLeft (a F), as a left adjoint, preserves finite colimits. Symmetry gives tensorLeft (a F) isomorphic to tensorRight (a F), transferring finite-colimit preservation. Combine with finite-limit preservation to obtain exactFunctor, precisely IsFlat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].
